2027-02-23.title: Tuesday of the third week of the Great Fast · St Polycarp of Smyrna
readings: Lot shelters the angels in Sodom
Come to me, all you that are weary
2027-02-23.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), third week. Commemoration of Mar Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna and martyr; name day of Mathews Mar Polycarpos.
2027-02-23.verse: Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
theo: Today we remember Mar Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, who as a young man had known St John the Apostle and who was burned for Christ in his old age, about the year 155. The account of his martyrdom, written by his own Church, tells how the proconsul urged him to curse Christ and save his life. Polycarp answered that for eighty-six years he had served Christ and had never been wronged by him: how could he blaspheme the King who had saved him? (in substance). He had carried the yoke of Christ for a lifetime and found it light. Paul explains why: “since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ… we also boast in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope does not disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit.” Polycarp's hope did not disappoint him.

The first reading is a dark night in Sodom. Lot sits in the gate and, like his uncle Abraham, insists on welcoming the two strangers: “he urged them strongly; so they turned aside to him and entered his house.” Then the men of the city surround the house with violence. Lot's response is itself a terrible wrong: he offers his own daughters to the mob. Scripture records it without approving it; it shows how deeply the sin of a city can twist even a man who wants to do right. It is not Lot who saves the day, but the guests: “the men inside reached out their hands and brought Lot into the house with them, and shut the door.” God's messengers pull him to safety. And Jesus opens another door to all who are crushed by the weight of sin and fear: “Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart.” Today we also pray for Mathews Mar Polycarpos on his name day.
outline: Ask: what burden are you carrying into this third week of the Fast?
Point 1 · A dark night in Sodom
The guests reach out and save Lot.
The gentle yoke, the martyr's rest.
“Come to me… and I will give you rest.”
live: Write down the heaviest burden you are carrying and leave it before the tabernacle or a holy picture today.
Accept one small hardship today without complaint, offering it for persecuted Christians.
2027-02-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, gentle and humble in heart, you call all who are weary to come to you. You gave Mar Polycarp the strength to serve you faithfully for eighty-six years and to die for you in hope. Pour your love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, so that our sufferings may produce endurance, character and hope. Pull us from every danger as your angels pulled Lot from the night, and give us your rest. Bless Mathews Mar Polycarpos on his name day. Amen.
altar: Polycarp prayed in the fire as one offering a sacrifice (in substance); at the altar we join the one Sacrifice of Christ that gives the martyrs their strength.

quick: Lot sheltered God's messengers, and they pulled him to safety from the violent crowd.
Suffering produces endurance, character and hope, and hope does not disappoint us.
Jesus invites all who are weary to come to him and find rest.
2027-02-23.action: Offer one hardship today for persecuted Christians.
2027-02-23.question: What heavy burden do I need to bring to Jesus?

family.explain: Jesus says: come to me, all who are tired and carrying heavy things, and I will give you rest. Today we remember St Polycarp, an old bishop who loved Jesus all his life. When he was told to say bad things about Jesus, he said: Jesus has always been good to me; how can I speak against him?
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “What is heavy in our hearts that we can give to Jesus tonight?”

illus: A porter at a railway station in Kollam carried other people's luggage for forty years. His back was bent and his knees were bad. When his grandson asked if he was ever tired, he laughed and said: always. But every morning before work he stopped at the church near the station for two minutes. What do you do there? the boy asked. He said: I put down my own load first. Then I can carry other people's.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we are weary and burdened. We come to you for rest. Amen.
share: The men inside reached out their hands and brought Lot into the house (Genesis 19:10). When has God pulled me back from danger?
Suffering produces endurance (Romans 5:3). How has a past suffering shaped my character?
I am gentle and humble in heart (Matthew 11:29). What do I need to learn from Jesus' gentleness?
interc: For Mathews Mar Polycarpos on his name day, and for all our bishops.
For Christians persecuted for their faith.
For the elderly who have served the Lord for many years.
For those caught in cities and places of violence.
For all who are weary and burdened.
pm.close: Father, you strengthened Mar Polycarp to bear witness to your Son in old age and in fire. Pour your love into our hearts, give us hope that does not disappoint, and lead us to the rest of Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we remember Mar Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, a disciple of St John. When the proconsul ordered him to curse Christ, he answered that he had served Christ for eighty-six years and had never been wronged; how could he blaspheme his King and Saviour? (in substance).

Paul tells us the secret of such faithfulness: suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope does not disappoint us, because God's love has been poured into our hearts (Romans 5:3–5).

In Sodom Lot welcomed God's messengers, but violence surrounded his house. It was the guests who saved him: the men inside reached out their hands and brought Lot into the house with them, and shut the door (Genesis 19:10). God reaches out to pull us from danger.

And Jesus says: come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me (Matthew 11:28–29). Let us bring our burdens to him in this Fast, as Polycarp did all his life. Amen.
kids: Children, St Polycarp was a very old bishop who loved Jesus. Bad men told him to say Jesus was not good. He said: Jesus has been good to me all my life! He was brave because he loved Jesus. Jesus says: come to me when you are tired, and I will help you.

intro: Theme: “Come to me… and I will give you rest.”
On the day of Mar Polycarp: God's hand that pulls us from danger, the hope that does not disappoint, and the rest of Christ.

sub: The guests reach out and shut the door.
q: For he will command his angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.
then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment until the day of judgment
points.apply: Thank God tonight for one time he rescued you from danger or sin.

q: but those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.
and hope does not disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us.
points.apply: Offer each hardship this week for Christians who suffer for the faith.

sub: Eighty-six years under the easy yoke.
q: Thus says the Lord: Stand at the crossroads, and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way lies; and walk in it, and find rest for your souls.
Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
points.apply: Make a short visit to the Blessed Sacrament each day this week to lay down your burden.

concl: God reaches into our darkest nights to pull us to safety.
Those who carry Christ's yoke, like Polycarp, find it light to the end.
2027-02-23.resolve: Bring your burdens to Christ each day of the Fast, and carry others' burdens with him.
